_meta.description: Machine-readable component map. Read before exploring the codebase. Update as part of every feature branch that adds or moves components.
_meta.upstream_debt_legend: Files/dirs still using HestiaCP-specific paths (/usr/local/hestia, /etc/hestiacp, hestia-nginx, hestia-php) that need migration to HestiaRE conventions.
_meta.os_targets: All four are first-class, equal-priority: debian-bookworm (12), debian-trixie (13), ubuntu-noble (24.04), ubuntu-26lts (26.04). load_os_profile (include/helper.sh) is the single source for OS_ID/CODENAME/RELEASE/EXIM_USR/BASE_PKGS_EXTRA. Every feature must work on all four; verify on the VM fleet before a PR.
_meta.distro_quirks: Cross-cutting gotchas that bite more than one service (grep these before assuming a service failure is your bug): (1) Ubuntu 26.04 ships ENFORCED AppArmor profiles that deny access other distros allow — proftpd can't read the panel cert under /usr/local/hestia/ssl (h-add-sys-proftpd drops share/proftpd/apparmor-local into the profile's local/ hook), and mariadbd's profile denies the dac_override the mariadb-install-db bootstrap needs (h-add-sys-mariadb unloads it for the init, reloads after). Suspect AppArmor on any 'Permission denied as root' on ub26. (2) Package names/splits differ by distro+version: proftpd-basic is bookworm-only (else proftpd-core), and modern proftpd (1.3.9 / 1.3.8 on trixie+ubuntu) moved mod_tls into proftpd-mod-crypto — omitting it silently disables FTPS. libzip is libzip4t64 on ub24 (t64 transition) but libzip5 on ub26. (3) apt-cache/apt-get output is localized — always LC_ALL=C before grepping for 'Candidate:' etc. (4) dovecot 2.3 (deb12) vs 2.4 (deb13/ub26) need version-split configs (share/dovecot/{2.3,2.4}/).
_meta.reference_docs: CLAUDE.md (rules), this map (component->files), PATHS.md (filesystem layout), BACKUP.md (the operator's view of backup and restore: modes, retention, adoption, remote targets, restic, exports, what the subsystem does NOT promise), UPDATE.md (the operator's view of updating: what a run does in order, what the run directory holds, the point of no return, and what the backup does NOT cover), and STRUCTURE.md (why the structure diverges from HestiaCP and what each divergence forces - read it before assuming why a subsystem was rebuilt: panel Caddy/Sury, the system-user split, protected downloads, webmail loopback, the FileManager/SFTP-jail rebuilds, /etc/hestia, and the permanent removals). Keep STRUCTURE.md current in the same PR as any structural change. Per-folder PROVENANCE.json (bin/, include/, web/, share/ - sbin/ has none: every file there is HestiaRE-native) tracks per-file upstream heritage + RAW churn divergence (triage only); complements VENDORED.json (third-party) and STRUCTURE.md; recompute is a manual, occasional job.

upstream_provenance.purpose: Maps HestiaRE files back to their HestiaCP origin so an upstream advisory or bugfix can be diffed against the right file. Fork point: HestiaCP 1.9.6, kept read-only in the upstream/hestiacp branch. Each component carries an `upstream_ref` using these tags.

tags.near-verbatim: upstream file, renamed and/or path-migrated (v-*->h-*, /etc/hestiacp->/etc/hestia) but logic intact - the cheapest file to compare an upstream change against, since our version is still close
tags.reimplemented: clean HestiaRE reimplementation that diverges from upstream - compare per function, not per file; the v-* symlink is usually removed (symlink_policy.escalation_rule)
tags.moved: upstream file relocated in-tree (mainly install/deb/* and install/common/* → share/*, #119) but otherwise near-verbatim
tags.removed: upstream component deleted from HestiaRE (bind9/DNS #58/#283, web terminal #59, REST API #146, SpamAssassin #284, software installer #56)
tags.hestiare-native: no upstream equivalent — HestiaRE-only (Caddy + hestia-php panel services, the pure-bash installer, panel Eigenbau libs, repo tooling)

upstream_provenance.verification_note: The #386 triage is a worked example, from when direct picks were still allowed: near-verbatim files (include/db.sh) took a helper verbatim, reimplemented ones (include/main.sh parse_object_kv_list, the search-object commands) were confirmed safe or ported by hand. Kept as history - today the answer would be 'port by hand' in both cases.

drift_watch.purpose: Machine-checkable per-file drift markers (#412). share/upstream/sync-upstream.sh reads this map and, after refreshing the upstream/hestiacp snapshot, flags any listed file that upstream MOVED since its checked_ref — so drift is caught deterministically, not by chance (the jailbash 5-bind drift behind `--tmpfs /usr/share` was a lucky find). checked_ref is the upstream/hestiacp commit the HestiaRE copy was last human-verified against; bump it ONLY after re-verifying the file against the newer upstream. upstream_path handles renames (v-*→h-*). A ref-stamp (not a flat ignore list) distinguishes 'deliberately diverged, verified at ref X' from 'not looked at yet'.

share/bubblewrap/jailbash.note: byte-identical to upstream at this ref (#412 re-sync of the 5 --tmpfs /usr/share binds)

upstream_provenance.adoption_rule: HestiaRE does not cherry-pick. Every adoption is a reimplementation, including isolated bugfixes, and every upstream change is challenged on its own: what the diff actually does (not the changelog title), whether we already have it or better, and whether it is worth the regression risk. Compare per function. These tags say how close our file still is - orientation for that comparison, never a merge plan. Always verify installed==fixed against the actual file, never the version string.

cli_commands.description: All CLI commands. h-* prefix is HestiaRE-native (renamed from v-* in Issue #22). v-* symlinks for HestiaCP compatibility added in Issue #23. No hl-* commands.

symlink_policy.baseline: Each h-* command that predated Issue #23 has one v-* symlink. New h-* commands created after Issue #23 get NO v-* symlink — the v-* name never existed.
symlink_policy.escalation_rule: When a command is substantially rewritten and diverges significantly from its HestiaCP upstream equivalent, its v-* symlink is removed. Rationale: prevent an upstream v-* command being mistaken for a drop-in equivalent of an internally incompatible implementation. Applied in Issue #54 (v-add-sys-roundcube removed after total rewrite for OS-package migration).
symlink_policy.deletion: When removing an h-* command: remove its v-* symlink too — no orphans.
symlink_policy.creation: Committed v-* symlinks ship in the tarball, so the installer does NOT blanket-create them (a `for h-* ; ln -s v-*` loop minted an orphan alias for every HestiaRE-native command, #123). configure_hestia only prunes dangling v-* (a `find -xtype l` — e.g. an alias left pointing at a renamed/removed h-*); h-check-sys-smoke check_v_symlinks_resolve guards against a dangling alias at runtime. No allowlist: an extra working alias for a native command is harmless and not worth maintaining a list for a compat layer meant to fade out.

file_roles.main.sh: Core utilities: source_conf(), check_result(), output formatting, logging, JSON/shell serialization. Object parsing: parse_object_kv_list (PHP tokenizer, quote-safe, single eval — the upstream double-eval RCE GHSA-w3mx is NOT present, empirically verified #386) and parse_object_kv_list_non_eval (declare -g, no eval — use this for any user-controlled conf-field payload). Input hardening from the HestiaCP 1.9.8 adoption (#471): include/sanitize_html.php (own dependency-free DOMDocument allow-list sanitizer for panel-rendered HTML - p/span/code/a/strong/br + safe href, drops script/on*/js:; used by h-add-user-notification since NOTICE renders via Alpine x-html), is_notification_topic/notice_valid (CR/LF + length guards on the single-line notifications.conf), and is_no_quote_format (blocks a single-quote/newline breaking out of a single-quoted field interpolated into the executed restore queue backup.pipe, GHSA-2xw3). SFTP jail membership helpers add_chroot_jail/delete_chroot_jail (#413: usermod -aG / gpasswd -d on the sftp-jailed group — the per-session jail itself is built by pam_namespace, see ssh_shell_jail.sftp_jail). manage_sshd_allowusers add|del <user> (#412): co-maintains the AllowUsers login allowlist in /etc/ssh/sshd_config for panel users — opt-in (acts only if an AllowUsers line exists; installer seeds one commented), edits ONLY the token whose base==user so operator entries (root@IP, maintenance) and the commented/active state survive, validates with `sshd -t` before swapping, reloads sshd only when active, re-comments rather than leaving an active line empty (lockout guard); called from h-add-user/h-delete-user AND rebuild_user (include/rebuild.sh) so restore/rebuild — which bypass h-add-user — re-add the user (else a restored user is missing from an active line and silently locked out). Family helpers for the whole tree (#602/#893): ip_family (by content, never by path), is_host46_format_valid (a remote host is a name OR a bare address) and url_host (brackets a v6 for a URL or an ssh-style host:path - NOT for the expect script in backup.sh, where Tcl needs them escaped, nor for the ftp client, which takes the address bare). HESTIA_RELEASE_MIRROR is the runtime twin of the two bootstrap literals; h-check-sys-smoke's check_release_mirror holds all three together.
file_roles.domain.sh: Domain validation and template checking for web and mail
file_roles.rebuild.sh: User and domain rebuild logic — regenerates service configs from HestiaRE data. Queue invariant: lines appended to conf/queue/*.pipe (run via `bash` by h-update-sys-queue) must contain only validated identifiers (username/domain), never free text (GHSA-47mf).
file_roles.syshealth.sh: System health monitoring, RRD graph generation, service status checks
file_roles.db.sh: MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL connection helpers, host configuration. Passwords entering SQL MUST go through mysql_sql_escape()/sql_escape() before 'IDENTIFIED BY'/'PASSWORD' literals (GHSA-8w7m, #386); no eval in this file.
file_roles.backup.sh: Local, FTP, and Restic backup/restore handlers with retention logic
file_roles.ip.sh: IP objects and their families (#602): ip6_canonical (RFC 5952 at the door), get_user_ips [family], get_user_ip = the v4 SLOT or empty (never a v6 - its callers write into IP fields and %ip% listen lines), get_user_ip6, get_ip_alias, and the increase/decrease counters whose ONE rule is h-update-sys-ip-counters <ip> check. ip_family() itself lives in main.sh, because web-model consumers do not source this file.
file_roles.docker.md: Per-user rootless Docker (#389). Host side: h-add-sys-docker / h-delete-sys-docker install docker-ce from the OFFICIAL repo (a scoped exception - neither Debian packages compose v2, the OS docker.io spans 20.10 to 29.1, and dockerd-rootless.sh ships only in Debian's build), disable the rootful daemon INCLUDING docker.socket (else socket activation resurrects it), and refuse on cgroup v1. Deliberately unpinned: no OS package shares a name with that repo. No cgroup delegation drop-in either - systemd already ships user@.service with Delegate=pids memory cpu on all four targets, and adding cpuset/io on the template would widen every session on the box. Customer side: h-add-user-docker creates the companion at uid-1000 with its OWN private group (the customer group would be caught by the customer home's group::--- ACL entry and never reach other::--x, so the companion could not traverse into its own home), writes the ORDER-SENSITIVE subuid/subgid triple that maps container 1000 to the customer, and starts the daemon with a group-owned socket in ~/.companion. Verified maps: 0->companion, 1000->customer. Traps: systemd-run --machine starts from a bare environment and the rootless setuptool refuses without HOME; the setuptool already starts the daemon, so its exit code is NOT the verdict and a later `enable --now` is a no-op; a restored home arrives with the unit enabled and the previous host's override, so its dead-socket start latches systemd's rate limiter and needs reset-failed. Liveness is proved by asking the API, never by [ -S ] on the socket file, which survives the daemon that made it. Backups exclude ~/.companion/.local/share/docker (images are pulled); h-restore-user re-owns the tree to the new companion uid BEFORE re-enabling, since tar cannot map it by name when the account does not exist yet.
file_roles.identity.sh: Panel user identity ALLOCATION (#388), not derivation. The username hash only picks where to start looking; the first free slot wins and stays that user's uid, as in classic HestiaCP. Interleaved 1000-blocks: customers in the odd thousands (11000-41999), each companion in the block below (10000-40999), 16000 slots, sub_base = 100000 + k*65536, disjoint by construction and below 2^31. A taken slot is not an error - identity_allocate reprobes with H(username:n). Backups carry NO authoritative identity and restores allocate fresh: portability comes from tar resolving ownership by NAME on extract (verified - a file archived as uid 5001 lands on 5099 once the name maps there), which is why the account is created BEFORE the unpack and why h-backup-user must never gain --numeric-owner. The only case still needing a chown is a restore under a different username, where tar finds no local name and falls back to the archived numbers; the inherited old_uid/new_uid re-chown in h-restore-user covers it. Paired with login_defs_guard (include/helper.sh), which caps UID_MAX/GID_MAX below the band and raises SUB_UID_MAX: the shipped default 600100000 sits below our highest range end (1048675999) and would otherwise reject roughly 43% of subordinate ranges.
file_roles.firewall.sh: Firewall renderer library - the ONE place that knows the backend's syntax. Renders the object model into a single nft `inet hestia` table. A batch buffers into sections and is assembled at apply time, because nft wants a document and because callers emit in a different order than the ruleset needs (jails are added last but must match first). One `nft -f` swaps the whole table after `nft -c -f` validates it, so there is no fail-open window and nothing half-applies. Dynamic sets render from source-of-truth files (fw_set_src) so a table replace cannot lose their contents; fw_set_replace does a live flush+refill in one transaction for the paths that must not rebuild everything. fw_legacy_teardown retires any iptables ruleset, which is mandatory because iptables is the nft shim and would otherwise keep being evaluated.
file_roles.sieve.sh: Everything that has to agree about sieve, because the engine and the two webmail clients are separate addons installable in any order: whether sieve is on (read from the record, not from this shell - a caller may have just written it through h-change-sys-config-value), the roundcube plugin list, Tachyon per-domain Sieve.enabled including default.json (which Tachyon clones for every domain added later), and the IMAP-learning chain - imap_sieve in the protocol mail_plugins, _rspamd-ctrl appended to dovecot mail_access_groups, and the compile step that must run AFTER the dovecot restart because sievec resolves sieve plugins through the running server (#780).
file_roles.sysreg.sh: Readers and the schema guard of the system key registry (share/hestia/sys-keys.json): sysreg_keys/class/default/tokens, sysreg_check. jq only, no other include - the same guard runs in the smoke and in CI (#932).

update_engine.description: The update building blocks and the derivation (#946 Phase 2, #947 Phase 3 of the update chapter). Conditions and actions are named functions behind one dispatcher, so a manifest entry is data and never shell. The derivation reads share/updates/*.json plus the box status and emits the plan that a run writes as update.conf; it executes nothing. update.sh is the run: it finds the release, fetches and verifies it, secures the tree into a run directory under /root, unpacks, derives the plan from the new tree and hands it to the executor. Its self-update comes first and is finished before anything on the box changes: the tarball the run needs anyway carries the newer updater, so one query answers both questions and the process exec's into it once, handing over tarball and run directory. Retention is unlimited and nothing prunes (E10); the run directory also holds rollback.sh, which restores the tree, hestia.conf and every saved path outside the tree, and refuses once the point-of-no-return marker exists. update.sh --check is also the writer of UPDATE_AVAILABLE for the panel banner, run daily from the one crontab writer. The executor (sbin/h-update-hestia) works that plan off. include/release.sh answers where a release comes from, for anything running on an installed box; install.sh keeps its own copy because it resolves a release before this tree exists, and the smoke holds the two mirror literals against each other. RELEASE_BRANCH is `release` (newest tag) or a vX.Y.Z pin, no channels, and h-change-sys-release refuses a pin the source does not carry. Since #948 nothing re-applies the outside-tree parts by itself: reapply_outside_tree is gone, the two unit re-applications belong to the release that changes the unit, and the two that have no tree counterpart (sudoers, login.defs) are reported by the smoke with the command that ends the drift. Boundary: a guard reports, an action writes. The lower bound UPDATE_MIN_VERSION in update.sh is v0.19.0: a box below it is reinstalled, not updated, and a target older than the installed tree is refused, in update.sh and in h-change-sys-release. The bound is compared against the TREE version, never the status: a run that unpacked but has not worked its plan off carries an older status on purpose and must stay able to finish. Because the literal travels in the tarball, the handover makes the target release's own bound the one that decides, before a file on the box is touched.
update_engine.guards: Two in the smoke, both derived from the code: the dispatcher's accepted name set against the defined upd_cond_*/upd_act_* functions (an empty derivation is red), and the structure of every shipped manifest through upd_manifest_check (file name against the version field, ids unique per file, every condition and action type known, the after graph resolvable and free of cycles, reversible within its action's bound). The manifest guard prints how many entries it read, because zero manifests is the honest state until Phase 5 and a green line must not read as coverage.
update_engine.quirks: An entry carries exactly ONE action: its reversibility is its action's, nothing folds over a set, and a mixed pair (file_copy plus service_restart) stays two entries so the reversible half can still run in front of the point of no return. reversible may be declared more pessimistic than the action type, never more optimistic; only the upper bound is a lie the guard has to catch. Every rc 2 a condition can return comes from the tree (unknown key, value outside the vocabulary), never from the box, so evaluating a condition is a structural check the smoke may run. The list is derived once before the run: an entry whose condition only becomes true because another entry ran is not in it, and after does not add it.

sys_key_registry.description: The system key registry (#932, Phase 1a of the update chapter): one entry per hestia.conf key with class and default. Since 1c (#944) share/manifest.json links every component to its key (status_key, status_token, status_artefact) and h-check-sys-smoke holds the link against the registry and the box. betreiber = a human sets it, the repair fills an absent/empty key with the default, an update never touches it. system = the consequence of a command, never filled by the repair; the smoke says whether it agrees with the box. Read at runtime from the tree on purpose (STRUCTURE.md, section 8).
sys_key_registry.guards: Three, one implementation twice called: (1) schema - unique names, class in {system, betreiber}, a default for betreiber and none for system, token_fn names a function that include/*.sh defines; (2) every key the tree writes into hestia.conf is registered - the write sites are extracted from the shipped code (wcv/_wcv, change_sys_value/clear_sys_value, h-change-sys-config-value with a literal key, direct echo/sed on hestia.conf, WEB_MODEL_KEYS), never listed; (3) an empty registry or an extraction under 20 keys is red. Not covered: a key written through a variable name.
sys_key_registry.quirks: The readers fail loudly and print nothing on a registry they cannot use; h-list-sys-config then ends non-zero and the login refuses (503) instead of gating on an empty session. conf/defaults/system.conf is no longer written (the seven object registries stay). Token keys (DB_SYSTEM, BACKUP_SYSTEM, WEBMAIL_SYSTEM) name sys_key_token_set in include/main.sh; 1a only guards that it exists, Phase 2 calls it. CRON_SYSTEM is betreiber with default cron and stays: it names the implementation, no command sets it, and the daily repair writes the default back, so the gates it feeds cannot go quietly permissive (#971). A key marked secret:true is emitted as a mask, never as its value - the panel writes every key to a session FILE; the one reader that needs the value takes 'h-list-sys-config secret KEY' (#976).

ssh_shell_jail.description: SSH/SFTP access control: the 3-tier access ladder — nologin (SFTP-only chroot, the default) · jailbash (bubblewrap-sandboxed interactive shell, opt-in) · bash (unconfined). #223 was the baseline check; the non-SFTP hardening landed in #412 (Story 1); the SFTP transport/chroot was rebuilt on pam_namespace in #413 (Story 2). See docs branch jail-chroot-story{1,2}-plan.md.
ssh_shell_jail.jailbash: share/bubblewrap/jailbash (moved from install/common/bubblewrap; deployed to /usr/sbin/jailbash by h-add-sys-ssh-jail) — bwrap wrapper run as the jailbash login shell: reuses host /usr read-only but with private /tmp,/home,/var,/run and stub passwd/group, --unshare-all (incl. pid → fresh /proc) --share-net. NEAR-VERBATIM UPSTREAM (origin/upstream/hestiacp) — tracked for drift (the #412 5-bind re-sync of zoneinfo/php/ca-certificates/i18n + /etc/php, lost behind `--tmpfs /usr/share`, was a chance find; a CI drift-gate is planned). Registered as a login shell in /etc/shells by h-add-sys-ssh-jail. NOTE: --share-net means 127.0.0.1 inside the jail is the HOST loopback (a jailbash user reaches host-bound services: redis:6379, webmail FPM :8090/:8091, panel, adminer) — an open isolation question tracked in Story 1 verification, not yet closed.
ssh_shell_jail.apparmor_userns_quirk: On Ubuntu 24.04+/kernels with apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, unprivileged user namespaces are blocked and bwrap fails without the `bwrap-userns-restrict` AppArmor profile (source: share/bubblewrap/bwrap-userns-restrict, deployed to /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict by h-add-sys-ssh-jail). That profile is installed ONLY when /etc/apparmor.d/abi/4.0 exists (the artefact-based guard, NOT an OS-version flag). Keep this rationale verbatim — hard-won.
ssh_shell_jail.shell_allowlist: include/main.sh HESTIA_SHELL_ALLOWLIST + list_allowed_shells (#412): the single curated source (nologin/jailbash/bash/sh ∩ /etc/shells, nologin guaranteed) shared by is_format_valid_shell (hard validator) AND h-list-sys-shells (the panel dropdown source for web/edit/user + web/{add,edit}/package). Dropped from upstream: rssh (gone from Debian, silently degrades to nologin), screen/tmux (useless as login shell), dash/rbash. The validator is genuinely hard (not a UI-only filter): h-change-user-shell gates every genuine change through it, EXCEPT re-asserting the user's current shell (in-allowlist OR ==current — so a legacy off-list shell a restore left in place can be re-set, but no new off-list shell slips in). rebuild.sh sets the shell straight from /etc/shells (bypasses the validator) so restore stays tolerant; the user/package editors render an existing off-allowlist shell as a selected "(current)" option so an unchanged save never resets it. FTP_SHELL (domain-FTP sub-accounts, h-add-web-domain-ftp/rebuild.sh) is a SECOND shell source that bypasses both panel and validator → Story 2.
ssh_shell_jail.allowusers: include/main.sh manage_sshd_allowusers add|del <user> — co-maintains an AllowUsers login allowlist in /etc/ssh/sshd_config; installer seeds it commented/inert. Panel users hooked in #412 (h-add-user/h-delete-user/rebuild_user); domain-FTP sub-accounts hooked in #413 (h-add-web-domain-ftp/h-delete-web-domain-ftp). See func_libraries.file_roles.main.sh for the full contract.
ssh_shell_jail.sftp_jail: pam_namespace SFTP jail (#413), replacing the old /srv/jail systemd bind-mount machinery. Per session, pam_namespace mounts a private tmpfs on /run/hestia/jail (from share/tmpfiles.d/hestia-jail.conf) and runs share/security/hestia-jail.init INSIDE the new mount namespace, as root, BEFORE sshd chroots: it builds the jail at the FIDELITY path (/run/hestia/jail/$user/<real-home>, from getent passwd) and bind-mounts the real home there — so ONE generic rule serves both panel users (home /home/$user) and domain-FTP sub-accounts (user-owned home deep under web/$domain, which native chroot cannot handle). fail-closed rides on sshd's own safely_chroot() (aborts if any chroot component is not root-owned or is group/other-writable): the fresh tmpfs root is 1777, the init builds everything while it is still 1777 and `chmod 755` on the root is the LAST action, so any failure leaves it 1777 → session refused (pam_namespace IGNORES the init exit code, so this is the real gate). Scope: the sftp-jailed group is BOTH the sshd chroot selector (one static `Match Group sftp-jailed` block) AND the PAM scope (`session [success=1 default=ignore] pam_succeed_if.so user notingroup sftp-jailed` before pam_namespace, so only members build a jail — non-members log in unchanged). Per user this is just group membership (add_chroot_jail=usermod -aG, delete_chroot_jail=gpasswd -d). No /home ownership flip (chroot root is root-owned in the tmpfs; the home keeps user ownership). No persistent state: no /srv/jail, no .mount units, no @reboot cron, no growing Match User list; /run/hestia/jail is tmpfs → self-heals on reboot via tmpfiles.d. Verified live on OpenSSH 9.2/9.6/10.0/10.2 (deb12/ub24/deb13/ub26), userns restriction active on ub26 with NO unprivileged userns/bwrap involved.
ssh_shell_jail.sftp_jail_quirks: Hard-won, non-obvious, expensive to rediscover — keep verbatim (same category as apparmor_userns_quirk): (1) pam_namespace IGNORES the iscript's exit code — fail-closed cannot ride on `exit 1`; it rides on sshd's safely_chroot() via the chmod-755-as-LAST-action on the still-1777 tmpfs root (any earlier failure leaves it world-writable → refused). (2) hestia-jail.init is a pam_namespace CALLBACK, never a standalone script: run by hand (even under `unshare -m`) it lacks slave-propagation, so `mount --bind` LEAKS the bind onto the host. Guarded by `mountpoint -q $polydir` (pam_namespace mounts the per-session tmpfs on the polydir before calling the iscript, so it is a mountpoint only in the real path; PAM_USER is NOT exported to the iscript, so it is not a usable discriminator — the mountpoint is). (3) A SKIPPED build (pam_namespace not firing at all) is still fail-closed: ChrootDirectory is always /run/hestia/jail/%u (never /home/%u), and that per-user dir exists only inside the per-session tmpfs → no build → missing dir → sshd refuses; it cannot resolve to the real home. (4) ForceCommand internal-sftp in the Match Group block forces SFTP even for a jailed user who has a real login shell (ssh-not-sftp → 'sftp connections only', no shell).

file_manager.description: Web file manager (#419 rebuild — replaces the old FileGator + SFTP-loopback connector). A per-customer php-fpm pool runs the app AS the customer, so the kernel UID is the file-access boundary (no connector, no keys, no crypto). Reached only via Panel-Caddy /fm/ → forward_auth → a private loopback listener → the customer pool. Baseline #218, integration concept #419. The app is a maintained fork of TinyFileManager 2.6 (single-file PHP), put on a diet: no external CDN — Bootstrap-CSS + a combined PrismJS build are vendored under share/filemanager/fm/assets/, FontAwesome (FA7) + (where needed) the panel's own assets are referenced same-origin; jQuery/Bootstrap-JS/DataTables/Dropzone/Ace/highlight.js are replaced by vanilla JS + a tiny Bootstrap-compatible modal/dropdown/tab shim, a native chunked uploader, native table filter/sort, and a Prism-overlay code editor (highlighting + line numbers, no preview). Vendoring is tracked in VENDORED.json (tinyfilemanager/prismjs/bootstrap-css) with upstream/* snapshot branches. Security note: the FM is SAME-ORIGIN with the panel (:8083/fm/), so any path that emits customer bytes is a panel-origin XSS surface — the ?media= handler therefore sets Content-Type ONLY from a server-side extension allowlist (never finfo/client), forces everything else (incl. SVG) to application/octet-stream + attachment, and always sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff + CSP default-src 'none'; sandbox; the third-party Google/MS doc-viewer iframes were removed (URL leak + broken off-box). Caddy drops all inbound X-Hestia-* (request_header -X-Hestia-*) before re-setting the trusted ones — the §7.2 invariant made structural. The FA4→FA7 icon remap covers the icons TFM actually references (fewer than a raw 1:1 of every upstream FA4 name; duplicates/unused dropped).
file_manager.two_hop: Caddy never talks to a customer FPM pool directly: an FPM socket is an interpreter (the client picks SCRIPT_FILENAME = code exec as the pool user), and www-data already has that reach over every customer pool (capability-neutral) whereas caddy (the phpMyAdmin/Roundcube user) does not — so /fm/ goes Caddy → nginx/apache private listener (as www-data) → the fm-<user> pool. nginx fronts it whenever it fronts the stack (nginx-only or nginx+apache); apache only in apache-only.
file_manager.auth: web/fm-auth.php is the ONLY authorization stop (the app runs with its own login disabled — the process is the tenant). Caddy /fm/* forward_auth → fm-auth.php (panel FPM, as hestia): a valid panel session → returns X-Hestia-User = the effective user (look/impersonation else session user). The 'enabled?' gate is the pool SOCKET's existence /run/hestia/fm/<user>.sock (a cheap stat — hestia CANNOT read /etc/hestia which is 700 root:root, so it does NOT read the FILE_MANAGER flag directly), which is the structural truth (no pool → no vhost → fail-closed).
file_manager.secret_invariant: The §7.2 invariant (guarded by the D6 smoke test): Caddy OVERWRITES two headers, never passing a client value — Host = fm-<user>.local (from the forward_auth response, selects the customer vhost) and X-Hestia-FM-Auth = the shared secret (/etc/hestia/conf/.filemanager.key, root:root 0600, baked into the caddy route at deploy time so caddy never reads the file). The private listener 403s without the secret and binds 127.0.0.1:FILE_MANAGER_PORT (8092) only.
file_manager.lifecycle: h-add-sys-filemanager deploys shared read-only code to /usr/share/filemanager/fm, generates the secret + tmpfiles socket dir + Caddy route, and reactivates saved per-user flags; h-delete-sys-filemanager reverses it but KEEPS per-user FILE_MANAGER flags (saved state, re-add reactivates). Per customer, h-add/delete-user-filemanager add/remove the pool (runs as the customer, pm=ondemand) + private vhost + FILE_MANAGER flag. rebuild_user (include/rebuild.sh) re-creates the pool+vhost for FILE_MANAGER=yes users — restore bypasses h-add-user-filemanager, so without it a restored user keeps the flag+menu but has no working FM (same lockout class as the AllowUsers fix 62eb1ca). h-add-user-filemanager waits for the pool socket before returning (no enable-time 403 race). Panel menu: h-list-user exposes the per-user FILE_MANAGER flag; top_panel() surfaces the EFFECTIVE (impersonation-aware) user's flag as $_SESSION['USER_FILE_MANAGER'] and web/templates/includes/panel.php gates the 'File manager' entry on it === 'yes' (its own key — never mixes with the legacy system-wide FileGator FILE_MANAGER).
file_manager.quirks: Hard-won, keep verbatim: (1) FILE_MANAGER must NOT be the last user.conf line — update_user_value deletes+reinserts by line number and a last-line key fails to reinsert (the address lands past EOF) and vanishes on the first toggle; it is inserted before TIME + seeded in rebuild's default block + registered in syshealth known_keys (where LOGIN_*/RATE_LIMIT are also still missing — pre-existing). (2) Stock TinyFileManager is NOT integration-ready — Phase-2 patches: P2 ($use_auth=false → trust forward_auth, else it shows its own login), P3 (root from getenv('FM_ROOT'), NOT $_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT'] which is /usr/share/filemanager, outside open_basedir → TFM echoes 'Root path not found'), P-selfurl (FM_SELF_URL/FM_ROOT_URL prepend HTTP_HOST = the internal routing host fm-<user>.local which the browser cannot resolve → make them relative). (3) FM app errors: the pool sets catch_workers_output=yes + log_errors=on, so they land in the php-fpm log tagged [pool fm-<user>]; TFM's own 'Root path' error is echoed to the page, not logged.
file_manager.status: Phases 1-4 done. Phase 1 (skeleton) + Phase 2 (vendored TFM diet) + Phase 4 (panel menu on the per-user flag + socket-wait) merged to dev; Phase 3 fleet-verified GREEN on deb12/deb13/ub24/ub26 (nginx path — all installs are PROXY_SYSTEM=nginx): secret gate 403/302, full panel session chain /fm/ 200 with the listing + 0 PHP fatals, pool runs as the customer, assets serve, edit/view/upload/media OK, theme passthrough (data-bs-theme) end-to-end. PENDING: the apache-only install profile (apache.tpl — needs a fresh apache-only build to exercise) + feinschliff (styling; FileGator-plumbing cleanup: legacy system FILE_MANAGER key, edit_server v_filemanager toggle, old /usr/local/hestia/web/fm tree, a module-installed menu gate).

upstream_ref.share/clamav/: install/deb/clamav/clamd.conf moved here (#123; deployed by h-add-sys-clamav — was orphaned; hardened LocalSocketMode 666→660 + LogVerbose off) plus two NEW curated files: socket-hardening.conf (systemd .socket drop-in) and apparmor-local. ClamAV is the antivirus analogue of rspamd: the exim `.ifdef CLAMD` block (av_scanner=clamd: + per-domain antivirus ACL + `deny malware=*/defer_ok`) was fully shipped but inert (macro commented). h-add-sys-clamav sets ANTIVIRUS_SYSTEM=clamav and arms the CLAMD macro ONLY after clamd answers on the socket (clamdscan --ping) — DB-download timeout leaves it OFF + honest WARN, because `defer_ok` is FAIL-OPEN (dead clamd → mail accepted UNSCANNED, not deferred), so an armed-but-blind macro would silently pass mail. THREE non-obvious wiring facts, all found in live testing: (1) BIDIRECTIONAL group membership — exim joins clamav (write the socket) AND clamav joins Debian-exim (READ /var/spool/exim4/scan, 0750 exim:exim); the second is load-bearing, without it clamd errors 'Permission denied' on the spool → fail-open passes mail unscanned. (2) The 660 socket is enforced by socket-hardening.conf (SocketMode=0660), NOT clamd.conf's LocalSocketMode — clamd is socket-activated so the clamav-daemon.socket unit owns the live /run/clamav/clamd.ctl mode (default 0666); the add script installs the drop-in + `systemctl restart clamav-daemon.socket`, and restarts the daemon (not enable --now) so it re-forks with the new group + socket. (3) apparmor-local re-asserts `/var/spool/exim4/** r,` into the clamd profile's local hook — the stock usr.sbin.clamd profile already grants it (0 denials on all 4 distros), this is defensive for a stricter base install; guarded on the profile file + `apparmor_parser … || true`, so a no-AppArmor host installs fine and the exim chain still scans (it relies on unix group perms, not AppArmor). Delete = saved-state (per-domain flags kept, restored on reinstall); the virus DB is moved aside across the purge and restored (apt purge clamav-freshclam wipes /var/lib/clamav) unless PURGE_DATA=yes, and the add script chowns it back to clamav in case the purge/reinstall re-allocated the uid. list_mail.php AV/spam columns now gate on ANTIVIRUS_SYSTEM/ANTISPAM_SYSTEM (neutral dash when the addon is gone).

APP→EXTENSION COUPLING (the reason the set is what it is): EVERY app on this single FPM master shares this one fpm conf.d — (1) panel UI web/, (2) phpMyAdmin+Adminer, (3) webmail Roundcube+Tachyon (#205). hestia-php-confd curates them as fpm_* / fpm_apps_* / fpm_webmail_* respectively. Non-obvious members: intl (webmail IDN), phar (Tachyon plugins), dom (Roundcube). make_release.description: Pure-bash installer. install.sh (bootstrap) → include/wizard.sh (manifest-driven Q&A → /etc/hestia/install.conf) → sbin/h-install-hestia (non-interactive, COMPONENT_*-gated). Migrated from Justfile/just/* to bash h-* commands in Issue #112 (epic); just removed (was Makefile→Justfile in #102, Justfile→bash in #112).

structure.install.sh: Bootstrap (curl-able): root + OS detect, apt prereqs (curl jq whiptail gnupg ca-certificates — no just), --dev source setup, fetch+extract release tarball, run include/wizard.sh, seed_hestia_etc, hand off to sbin/h-install-hestia.
structure.include/wizard.sh: Interactive whiptail wizard (bash fallback), manifest-driven: pre-questions + preset + dynamic version discovery + component questions; writes /etc/hestia/install.conf. Runnable standalone (hestia configure).
structure.include/helper.sh: hestia_apt (spinner + apt log split), load_os_profile (OS_ID/CODENAME/RELEASE/EXIM_USR/BASE_PKGS_EXTRA for deb12/deb13/ub24/ub26), seed_hestia_etc (hestia.env + profile.d + seed hestia.conf).
structure.sbin/h-install-hestia: Non-interactive orchestrator: validates /etc/hestia, sources hestia.env+main.sh+helper.sh+install.conf, runs stages gated by COMPONENT_*. Idempotent via .done.* sentinels (exit→return).
structure.sbin/hestia: Umbrella dispatcher: hestia install|configure|update|uninstall|status (no v-* alias).
structure.sbin/h-update-hestia: The executor (#948, phase 4 of the update chapter): takes the path to a run directory's update.conf and works the entries off through the dispatcher in include/update.sh. Finding, downloading, unpacking and securing a release is update.sh (phase 5), not this. Refuses when the run directory is missing, because that is where the backup and the rollback script live. The log goes into the run directory, never to a central file: it is evidence, and it is pruned with the run. Writes the point-of-no-return marker when it reaches the first irreversible entry, so a run that stops before it stays rollback-able. Epilogue only when the list is done: repair, object registries, status VERSION from the tree, UPDATE_AVAILABLE cleared, panel started.
structure.sbin/h-uninstall-hestia: Conservative uninstall (keeps /home + DBs always; --purge removes packages + /usr/local/hestia + /etc/hestia).
structure.bin/h-list-sys-install: Status report: version, source, OS, profile, .done.* phases, COMPONENT_*.

stages.install_base: APT repos (Sury always; MariaDB only for an external-repo version), base packages, system users, SSH hardening (Subsystem internal-sftp, LoginGraceTime 1m, DebianBanner no, and a commented #AllowUsers allowlist seed co-maintained by manage_sshd_allowusers, #412), NTP, /proc hardening via proc_hardening_apply (include/helper.sh: hidepid persisted via the hestia-proc-hardening.service unit from share/security/systemd, replacing the @reboot cron; NOT fstab - the systemd fstab generator skips API filesystems so a /proc line there is inert; skipped in containers where the remount is refused, re-asserted on upgrade from reapply_outside_tree). The unit resolves the procvis gid from /etc/group on every start rather than carrying an install-time value, so a deleted+recycled gid cannot silently exempt a foreign group; gid=0 when the group is absent, which is also how a stale exemption is withdrawn (a remount that merely omits gid keeps the old value). hidepid=invisible is required, not a preference: noaccess leaves foreign pids enumerable with their owners (156 vs 3 measured) AND still breaks rootless Docker. h-check-sys-smoke check_proc_hardening verifies the live mount, since failure is fail-open
stages.install_web: nginx + apache2 per WEB_SERVER with port model #247 (BOTH: nginx proxy 80/443 -> apache2 8080/8443; APACHE/NGINX alone: 80/443; Listen per IP via h-add-sys-ip, ports.conf emptied, mod_remoteip for client IP behind proxy), multi-PHP via COMPONENT_PHP_MULTIPHP_VERSIONS when sury_multi, web pool
stages.install_db: MariaDB (version from COMPONENT_DB_MARIADB_VERSION); phpMyAdmin/PostgreSQL/Redis per components
stages.install_mail: exim4, dovecot (version-aware), rspamd (optional), webmailers from the COMPONENT_MAIL_WEBMAILER token set (wizard checklist; roundcube fatal, tachyon degrades loudly, empty = none) — only if COMPONENT_MAIL_BLOCK_PRESENT
stages.install_security: nftables only (iptables and ipset are gone with the old renderer, #548); fail2ban (optional); crowdsec (optional, minimal - #123)
stages.install_addons: proftpd (→ h-add-sys-proftpd) / docker / filemanager per components (#123)
stages.configure_hestia: sudoers, v-* dangling-symlink prune, SSL cert, admin user, firewall, default domain, crontab; writes .done.configure
stages.install_tools: always-installed utilities + selected TOOLS_SELECTION + composer (source per COMPONENT_ADDON_COMPOSER_SOURCE: os_package default, upstream_installer on latest; h-update-sys-composer switches live, #208/#237) + wp-cli (manifest-pinned phar via fetch_wp_cli_phar)
stages.finalize_install: start hestia.service, schedule LE host cert, final apt upgrade, print credentials

make_release.sentinel_files: /etc/hestia/.done.{base,panel,web,db,mail,security,addons,configure} — presence skips that stage (return 0, NOT exit)
make_release.presets: 6 manifest presets (standard/compact/latest/singlephp/nomail/mailonly) drive COMPONENT_* in the wizard; h-install-hestia consumes COMPONENT_* directly (no profile-name dispatch). No custom preset on purpose (#195) - a config beyond every preset = hand-written install.conf
make_release.bootstrap_flow: curl | bash install.sh → OS detect → apt prereqs → download+extract tarball → include/wizard.sh → seed_hestia_etc → sbin/h-install-hestia
make_release.install_conf: /etc/hestia/install.conf — the RECIPE, written by include/wizard.sh and by nothing else afterwards (#945): HESTIA_* params, COMPONENT_* selections and the INSTALL_DATE/INSTALL_VERSION stamps, all in one write. A `type: fixed` component writes NO line (it is not a choice); the one exception marks itself with `recipe_line` in the manifest, and today that is only PANEL_EXIM, whose key the installer reads to skip the local MTA for a relay-only box. Sourced by h-install-hestia. No update ever rewrites it, so a box keeps the key set it was installed with and no reader may treat an absent key as a statement; what the box HAS is hestia.conf. hestia configure refuses on an installed box without --force (E22). Until 1d the h-add-*/h-delete-* commands kept COMPONENT_* current via set_install_component; that function and its 34 call sites are gone.
make_release.upstream_ref: hestiare-native — the whole installer (install.sh, include/wizard.sh, sbin/h-install-hestia, include/helper.sh) was rebuilt from scratch (Makefile→just→bash, #106/#112/#114); upstream's install/hst-install-*.sh were removed (#26). No upstream counterpart.
