web_botlimit.description: Server-native web bot rate-limiting, Layer B (#482) - a standalone subsystem, independent of CrowdSec and available on ANY web install (nginx-only, apache-only, both). Throttles bot families with native nginx limit_req / apache mod_qos and answers 429; humans are NEVER limited and malicious traffic stays CrowdSec's job (ban -> 403), so the two never overlap. Driven by an admin family table (share/botpolicy/botfamilies.conf seeded to /etc/hestia/botfamilies.conf, 8 curated families + 2 free slots, capped at 10 because each family costs two limit_req zones plus one more alternative in the per-request UA map). Per family: UA match + lenient/strict rate + enabled, plus conf-only advanced burst/nodelay. Per domain each family is off/lenient/strict via the web.conf BOTLIMIT field, rendered into a per-vhost fragment the templates include by glob (absent = no-op). nginx keys per family PER DOMAIN ($host:family, set inside the map VALUE so a non-bot UA still maps to "" and stays unlimited) - a busy customer's crawlers cannot 429 another customer out of a shared bucket; apache mod_qos counts per client IP - QS_ClientEventLimitCount blocks the WHOLE client IP for the rest of the window once a limit trips, so on an apache-only box a bot sharing a NAT address with real users takes those users down with it (measured 2026-08-03: 10/10 x 200 on nginx right after a limited bot, continuous 429 on apache). mod_qos has no limiter that counts only the matching requests, so this is a documented asymmetry, not a bug. Default off/opt-in. KNOWN LIMITATION: families match on the spoofable User-Agent and Layer B does not verify it (no rDNS/IP check), so on a non-CrowdSec install a client faking a crawler UA can drain that family's bucket; on CrowdSec installs the good-actor whitelist verifies real crawlers by rDNS/IP. INVARIANT: the server config defines zones only for ENABLED families, so a fragment must never reference a gone/disabled one - nginx -t would fail and block the next reload for the whole box; the fragment renderer skips them, the apply command re-renders every throttled domain first, and deleting a family also strips it from every domain.
web_botlimit.core: include/botpolicy.sh (botpolicy_seed_families, botpolicy_render_nginx/_apache, botpolicy_apply, botpolicy_render_domain_fragment, botpolicy_render_all_fragments, botpolicy_purge_family, botpolicy_rate_to_qos)
web_botlimit.config: /etc/hestia/botfamilies.conf (instance copy, survives updates) -> /etc/nginx/conf.d/hestia_botlimit.conf or /etc/apache2/conf.d/hestia_botlimit.conf (both GENERATED); per-domain $HOMEDIR/$user/conf/web/$domain/nginx.botlimit.conf | botlimit.apache2.conf
web_botlimit.panel: the family table is inline on Server Settings (web/edit/server/, admin-only, 10 slots saved with the settings form: APPLY=no per row + a single apply at the end; placement provisional pending the panel overhaul) + the Bot Rate Limiting section in web/edit/web/ (per-domain off/lenient/strict for the admin-ENABLED families, customer-editable and also settable by an admin while impersonating; only the family table stays admin-only. A customer cannot reach another tenant: the panel passes the effective session user and the CLI validates the domain against that user's own object file. Disabled families and unused slots never appear). h-list-web-domain exposes BOTLIMIT so the panel can see a domain's own levels.
web_botlimit.templates: templates/web/nginx/* include nginx.botlimit.conf*; templates/web/apache2/* include botlimit.apache2.conf* (Layer A keeps its own nginx.crowdsec.conf*)
web_botlimit.rebuild: include/rebuild.sh calls botpolicy_render_domain_fragment beside the CrowdSec Layer-A fragment
web_botlimit.no_symlink: new h-* commands, no v-* symlink

crowdsec.description: CrowdSec integration (#186), nginx-front only, in four layers. Layer A (L7): own dependency-free LuaJIT ban-bouncer that queries the local LAPI live and answers 403; rendered per web model + a per-domain fragment. L3: own cscli->ipset feeder (bin/h-update-firewall-crowdsec, timer-driven) fills a hestia-crowdsec DROP chain via h-update-firewall - the OS crowdsec-firewall-bouncer 0.0.25 is fleet-unusable (nil-panics in nftablesConfig). The feeder DENYLISTS scenario tokens so only web-tier bans normally reach the firewall; the auth families (ssh/ftp/mail/db) are denied only while fail2ban is present (FIREWALL_EXTENSION) - in the crowdsec-only model they reach L3 too (best-effort SSH/web enforcement, #498), while req-limit stays denied in every model so a Layer-B 429 never escalates. Fleet-mesh: peer-mesh shared blocklist, no central LAPI - each box publishes its own local bans and imports the union of its peers' as L7-only mesh bans (origin cscli-import, scenario hestia-mesh:<peer>); enforcement falls out for free (the L7 bouncer sees imported decisions, the L3 feeder filters origin==crowdsec). Packaged as a removable addon (#123). The LAPI is loopback-only (127.0.0.1:8054) throughout. Layer-B bot rate-limiting was decoupled into its own always-available subsystem (include/botpolicy.sh, #482) - CrowdSec bans, botpolicy throttles, and the two never overlap. crowdsec_apply removes crowdsecurity/nginx-req-limit-exceeded on purpose: it would escalate our own 429s into bans.
crowdsec.core: include/crowdsec.sh (engine install, Layer-A bouncer + per-model/per-domain rendering), include/crowdsec-mesh.sh (peering + pull transport helpers)
crowdsec.model: Three models, asked once in the wizard as CROWDSEC_MODE and switchable at runtime with h-change-sys-crowdsec-mode (#494): capi = central community blocklist + telemetry; local = self-hosted engine only; mesh = local plus the peer exchange, so mesh always disables the CAPI online_client. The LIVE model is derived from artefacts (is online_client commented out? does /etc/hestia/crowdsec/mesh.conf exist?) via crowdsec_current_mode - COMPONENT_CROWDSEC_MODE in install.conf is the install recipe, not live state; since #945 crowdsec_apply takes the mode as an ARGUMENT (installer hands over the recipe, h-add-sys-crowdsec the box) instead of sourcing install.conf inside the library. crowdsec_enable_capi is the inverse of crowdsec_disable_capi and rolls back to local if enrolment fails, because cscli capi register (1.4.x) loads the credentials file before writing it and so needs both an uncommented online_client AND an existing (possibly empty) file.
crowdsec.mesh_transport: Authenticated pull over the panel port (#485): web/mesh-decisions.php serves this box's published ban list behind a per-peer bearer token; web/mesh-pair.php completes a pairing that the peer initiated with a one-time code minted here. A pairing therefore needs an admin on BOTH boxes (initiating needs root/admin there, minting the code needs root/admin here) and /mesh-pair.php is a plain 404 while no code is live. TLS is pinned per peer (SPKI, TOFU at pairing) since panel certs are usually self-signed; each side installs an IP-scoped ACCEPT rule for the other on the panel port (never narrowing :8083 to peers-only). Secrets never ride in argv (/proc is world-readable): the panel hands payloads over in 0600 files under /run/hestia/mesh/in, curl reads tokens from a 0600 config, and only token HASHES are staged for the panel to compare (it runs as hestia and cannot read /etc/hestia).
crowdsec.config: /etc/hestia/crowdsec/{mesh.conf,peers.conf,pairing.conf} (root 0600; mesh.conf presence = mesh on), /run/hestia/mesh/{published.json,tokens,in} (panel-readable staging, tmpfiles.d + refilled by the timer)
crowdsec.panel: web/list/firewall/mesh/ + web/add/firewall/mesh/ + web/delete/firewall/mesh/ + web/generate/mesh-pairing/ (admin-only Fleet Mesh page: peers, shared-ban counts, generate/enter a pairing code)
crowdsec.timers: hestia-crowdsec-l3.timer (ipset feeder), hestia-crowdsec-mesh.timer (publish + pull + swap-import; the import is skipped while the union is unchanged and the decisions' TTL is still fresh)
crowdsec.smoke_guards: bin/h-check-sys-smoke (L3 + mesh timer checks, both artefact-gated)
crowdsec.no_symlink: new h-* commands, no v-* symlink

firewall.description: Host firewall, rebuilt on nftables in #495. include/firewall.sh is the sole owner of backend syntax and bin/h-update-firewall the sole full-ruleset writer: it renders one inet hestia table and applies it as a single atomic nft -f document, validated with nft -c -f first. Base chains carry hook + priority so foreign tables (fail2ban's own, a future bouncer's) coexist instead of fighting over INPUT. Sets render from their source files rather than from the live set, so a wholesale table replace cannot lose contents. iptables is xtables-nft-multi on all four targets, which means a leftover iptables ruleset is STILL EVALUATED by the same kernel backend - legacy teardown is mandatory, not housekeeping. inet covers v4 and v6 and loads on a host with no IPv6 configured, which is what lays the v6 groundwork without presupposing it.
firewall.object_model: /etc/hestia/firewall/{rules.conf,chains.conf,banlist.conf,ipset.conf,excludes.conf,crowdsec.conf,custom.sh} - abstract and renderer-independent, which is why the nftables migration keeps it and replaces only the marshalling. custom.sh is an operator escape hatch bashed after every apply. excludes.conf is the whitelist and is currently READ at exactly one place (h-add-firewall-ban, where it suppresses new bans) and WRITTEN BY NOTHING - no command, no panel page, no shipped default.
firewall.persistence: The applied document IS the persisted one: fw_batch_apply writes /etc/hestia/firewall/ruleset.nft and hestia-nftables.service (rendered whole by fw_boot_unit_write, never appended; deliberately not the dpkg conffile /etc/nftables.conf) reloads exactly that file at boot in one transaction - no save step, no dump post-processing, sets load with their rules atomically. h-check-sys-smoke guards it via check_firewall_closed and check_firewall_ruleset_loadable (plus backend/chains_tracked/rules_rendered/ipsets_populated/icmpv6).
firewall.blocklists: Lists referenced from a normal rule as IP='ipset:<name>'; the operator picks the ACTION, so a list is advisory rather than implicitly a DROP. Sources come from share/firewall/blocklists.conf (FireHOL L1/L2, Spamhaus DROP, Blocklist.de), read by the panel picker, so adding one is a data change (#481) - it replaced a shipped preset pointing at install/common/firewall/ipset/blacklist.sh, a path dissolved with the install/ tree in #119, which failed on the minimum-size check with a misleading error. Refresh runs off hestia-blocklist.timer (Persistent=true, RandomizedDelaySec=30min) rather than queue/daily.pipe, with the interval set by h-change-sys-blocklist-interval. nft interval sets carry auto-merge, so overlapping CIDRs collapse on load (1665 Spamhaus CIDRs -> 1509 elements) and the live element count will not match the source count. #510 tracks a dynamic picker with per-list size and age.
firewall.core: include/firewall.sh is the renderer library (#495); every backend call in bin/ and include/ goes through it - a repo-wide sweep for direct iptables invocation outside that file returns nothing.
firewall.smoke_guards: bin/h-check-sys-smoke: check_firewall_closed (INPUT policy must be DROP while FIREWALL_SYSTEM is set) and check_firewall_sets_bootable (every --match-set in the PERSISTED ruleset must have a boot provisioning path). The second reads the saved file on purpose - the kernel refuses --match-set for a nonexistent set, so a live dangling reference cannot exist and checking for one would always pass.
firewall.config_keys: FIREWALL_SYSTEM (nftables|empty - the VALUE changed in #495; renaming it left six sites comparing against the old 'iptables' literal, one of which let the panel destroy the live ruleset) gates every h-*-firewall* command via is_system_enabled and has h-add-sys-firewall/h-delete-sys-firewall plus a panel toggle. FIREWALL_EXTENSION (fail2ban|empty) is written ONLY by the installer and never cleared, so fail2ban cannot be turned off - see the fail2ban component and #497.
firewall.panel: web/{list,add,edit,delete,bulk,move,suspend,unsuspend}/firewall/ - rules, banlist, whitelist (exclude/), jail status (jail/), ipset, mesh. The whitelist page is NOT gated on FIREWALL_EXTENSION: it renders as a firewall accept and works without fail2ban, which is also what makes it the way back in after a lockout.
firewall.roadmap: Umbrella #481 (also Stage 0: the reference captures under firewall-captures/ on the docs branch are the equivalence reference for the renderer swap). #495 nftables renderer + native sets, #496 fail2ban, #497 fail2ban as an addon, #498 model matrix. Plans: firewall-roadmap.md + firewall-subsystem-analysis.md + nftables-migration-plan.md on the docs branch. Known defects D1-D8 are catalogued in the analysis doc.

project_quota.description: Project quota for /home (#211): base behaviour, no wizard item, no panel switch. The installer arms whenever the filesystem supports it; hestia.conf PROJECT_QUOTA (active|pending:<reason>|none:<reason>) is written from the enforcement probe, never from classification. ext4 needs quotaon -P at every boot (persistent unit) and offline superblock features (one-shot initramfs premount hook across the install reboot); xfs is mount-option-only (fstab or GRUB rootflags), remount is a silent no-op on both. Per-user application (project id = uid) lives in the stage-2 rework of h-update-user-quota.

customer_php_limit.description: Customer PHP CPU cap (#212): all customer php-fpm masters run in hestia-customer-php.slice via a per-version drop-in (/etc/systemd/system/php<v>-fpm.service.d/hestia-slice.conf, Wants=+After= the oneshot so no master starts uncapped). System protection, not a per-customer limit - it caps the customers together against panel, mail, database and ssh. The panel PHP is its own master (hestia-php.service, /etc/php/hestia) and stays outside; the fm-<user> filemanager pools live in the customer master and are inside. /etc/hestia/limits.conf carries CUSTOMER_PHP_CPU_PERCENT (share of the WHOLE machine, 10-100, seeded once and never rewritten); sbin/hestia-customer-php-limit is the single writer for both halves - it (re-)writes the drop-ins AND multiplies the share by nproc --all at every boot, because systemd counts CPUQuota per core, applying it with set-property --runtime so nothing absolute is stored and a box that gains cores grows its cap. There is deliberately no h-* command: customer_php_limit_apply (include/limits.sh) installs the units and seeds the conf, then triggers the unit, and 'systemctl restart hestia-customer-php-limit' is the repair path. The boot script always exits 0 so a broken cap cannot block a boot, but that is not fail-open: what survives is the slice unit's FIXED 200%, barely a limit on two cores and a hard sixth of a sixteen-core box - arbitrary rather than safe, which is why h-check-sys-smoke check_customer_php_slice reports the LIVE cgroup value and reads the percentage through the same range-checked customer_php_percent the boot script uses. Replaced the cgroup switch RESOURCES_LIMIT, which set properties on user-<uid>.slice that php-fpm workers never enter.

fail2ban.description: Brute-force protection, wired as a CLIENT of the hestia firewall rather than as an independent writer: share/fail2ban/action.d/hestia.conf maps actionstart/stop/ban/unban onto h-add/delete-firewall-chain and h-add/delete-firewall-ban, so bans land in banlist.conf AND in the live fail2ban-<CHAIN> chain and therefore survive a full h-update-firewall rebuild. That client model is the reason to keep owning the ban action rather than adopting fail2ban's native nftables banaction, which would bypass the banlist, the panel and rebuild-survival alike.
fail2ban.config_install: fail2ban_apply in include/fail2ban.sh is the single implementation of "a configured fail2ban", shared by the installer and (later) the addon commands. It copies the WHOLE share/fail2ban tree through a staging dir: enumerating the files individually is what once left out action.d/hestia.conf and made every jail using action = hestia[...] unstartable with smoke still green (D1, fixed in #502). Our jails live in jail.d/hestia.local, never in jail.local, which is left to the admin - fail2ban reads jail.conf -> jail.d/*.conf -> jail.local -> jail.d/*.local, so ours is read last and wins. The distro [sshd] jail is disabled from our own config rather than by deleting jail.d/defaults-debian.conf: that is a dpkg conffile, so rm -f is undone by the next package update.
fail2ban.jails: share/fail2ban/jail.local ships ssh, exim, dovecot, proftpd, hestia-panel, phpmyadmin, the four web-log jails (web-botsearch, web-badactor, web-exploit, web-authprobe), roundcube-auth, tachyon-auth and recidive. The web-* four are the L7 layer (#531): web-botsearch bans 404-enumeration on the botsearch vocabulary (rate, maxretry 10), web-badactor bans secret/config file-discovery paths, web-exploit bans traversal/RCE/appliance payloads (both status-agnostic, maxretry 2), web-authprobe bans repeated 401 (401-only; maxretry 20 because it counts per source IP AGGREGATED across all vhosts, not per domain). All L7 jails are signature/behaviour based, never rate - that is Layer B's job (include/botpolicy.sh) and its 429s must never escalate to a ban. They are gated together as one set (include/fail2ban.sh F2B_WEB_JAILS): fail2ban_gate_web_jail repoints their logpath at the configured web system, fail2ban_watch_domain addlogpath/dellogpath's each domain across all of them, and a per-filter smoke canary (check_fail2ban_web_signatures via fail2ban-regex) pins match+reject. Mail jails are gated on the mail model, proftpd on FTP_SYSTEM, the web jails on WEB_SYSTEM, and the two webmail jails on WEBMAIL_SYSTEM (each client independently) - a jail whose logpath does not exist never fires and says so only in fail2ban's own log. No mysqld jail on purpose: 3306 is not in the shipped ruleset, so it is loopback-only and h-add-firewall-ban would refuse to ban what could reach it. recidive covers ports 1:65535 and is what gives whole-box escalation - CrowdSec has no analogue today. Whitelisting is NOT configured here: h-add-firewall-exclude maintains it and mirrors it into jail.d/hestia-zz-whitelist.local.
fail2ban.hazards: fail2ban expands a logpath GLOB once, when the jail starts, and never again - a web domain added later is simply not watched, silently, until the daemon restarts. So h-add-web-domain, h-delete-web-domain, h-change-web-domain-name and rebuild_web_domain_conf all call fail2ban_watch_domain, which uses addlogpath/dellogpath to touch just that jail's file list without a reload. The web jail deliberately does NOT act on the rate limiter's 429s: Layer B (nginx limit_req / apache mod_qos) throttles bots itself and its verdicts must not escalate into firewall bans. Historic, all fixed: actionstop wiping the banlist and the multiport delete asymmetry (D4, #502), the dead unban grep (D6, withdrawn - the action really is named hestia-<CHAIN>), IPv4-only ban validation (D7, #506).
fail2ban.modularity: A removable addon like proftpd/clamav/crowdsec (#497): h-add-sys-fail2ban installs the package, sets FIREWALL_EXTENSION and runs the shared fail2ban_apply; h-delete-sys-fail2ban runs fail2ban_teardown (stop daemon, drop every chain from chains.conf via h-delete-firewall-chain, remove our config), clears FIREWALL_EXTENSION, re-renders the ruleset and purges the package. One live truth, FIREWALL_EXTENSION (hestia.conf): it gates runtime, renderer, panel, services and, since #945, the smoke block too; $_SESSION mirrors it for the panel. COMPONENT_ADDON_FAIL2BAN is the install-time answer and gates nothing at runtime any more. add refuses without FIREWALL_SYSTEM active (the ban action needs a ruleset); no saved state - our config re-renders from share/, the admin's jail.local is untouched. Panel toggle sits next to the firewall one in edit/server.
fail2ban.demarcation_with_crowdsec: The distro crowdsec package's own postinst installs crowdsecurity/linux + crowdsecurity/sshd and acquires /var/log/auth.log, so CrowdSec DOES detect SSH brute force. The L3 feeder's auth-family denylist keeps those decisions off L3 only WHILE fail2ban is present, so fail2ban owns SSH enforcement (~1s, cuts live connections) in the fail2ban and fail2ban+crowdsec models. In the crowdsec-only model (#498) fail2ban is gone and the feeder lets the auth families through to L3 - best-effort, ~45s latency, connections not cut. Mail still has no CrowdSec detection surface (no exim/dovecot collections), so crowdsec-only leaves mail brute force unprotected: a documented best-effort gap. The model is switched at runtime with h-change-sys-firewall-model, which derives the current model from the artefacts and orchestrates the two addon commands.
fail2ban.panel: web/list/firewall/banlist/ + add/delete/bulk, and web/list/firewall/jail/ for jail status (h-list-firewall-jail). The banlist merges fail2ban bans (banlist.conf) with CrowdSec local L3 decisions (h-list-firewall-crowdsec-ban, origin==crowdsec only) source-tagged, and unban routes by source (fail2ban -> h-delete-firewall-ban; crowdsec -> h-delete-firewall-crowdsec-ban); bulk value is source|ip|chain (a pipe, so IPv6 colons don't mis-split) (#527). The banlist button shows when FIREWALL_EXTENSION is set OR a CROWDSEC session signal is present (h-list-sys-config derives it from the L3 marker, so the button appears in the crowdsec-only model); jail status stays gated on FIREWALL_EXTENSION. The status page reports the jails our config enables UNION the jails fail2ban is running, so one that is configured but not running reads as stopped instead of vanishing - that gap is the reason it exists.
fail2ban.roadmap: Firewall roadmap Stages 0-4 delivered: #496 (fix + jail rework, whitelist page, jail-status view), #497 (removable addon), #498 (model matrix). The four models (none / fail2ban / fail2ban+crowdsec / crowdsec) are encoded by the two existing wizard checkboxes (crowdsec hidden on apache), switched at runtime by h-change-sys-firewall-model. crowdsec-only enforcement is best-effort (SSH/web to L3, mail detection still absent). Supersedes #236.
fail2ban.webmail_ip_chain: The webmail jails read the client IP through the panel-Caddy hop, which overwrites X-Forwarded-For to 127.0.0.1. Roundcube reads X-Real-IP (proxy_whitelist=127.0.0.1, log_logins), Tachyon reads Client-IP (auth_logging, labs http_client_ip_check_proxy) - the webmail vhost sets both from $remote_addr so neither is forgeable. Roundcube logs the user field verbatim, so its filter anchors the real trailer to end-of-line and lets a greedy user match backtrack to the genuine IP block (username log-injection defence, verified). #515.

web_model_switch.description: Live web-serving model switch (#120): change a running server between nginx-only / both / apache-only (previously install-only). Four thin commands - h-add-sys-nginx, h-add-sys-apache2, h-delete-sys-nginx, h-delete-sys-apache2 - over one shared core in include/web-model.sh; the model is DERIVED from the configured component set (WEB_SYSTEM/PROXY_SYSTEM in hestia.conf, never dpkg). Apply order: acquire the exclusive freeze lock -> durable snapshot + crash sentinel -> configure_apache2 (if target uses apache) -> flip keyset (change + clear) -> mod_remoteip toggle (enable for both incl. NAT IPs, disable otherwise) -> rebuild per-IP + web + webmail -> clean old-model artifacts -> validate (nginx -t / apache2ctl configtest + inventory assertion) -> stop the departing server, then enable+restart the target's servers (port handover). Explicit rollback (restore snapshot + re-start/enable) on any failure; --recover restores from an interrupted run's sentinel snapshot. The freeze: h-restart-web/-proxy/-service defer, 47 web/mail-vhost mutators + the LE renewal acquire the lock (bounded + reentrant via HESTIA_WEB_LOCK_HELD), apache logrotate skips its reload while held. Backups carry a WEB_SYSTEM/PROXY_SYSTEM marker (backup.conf + hestia/web-system in the archive); restore prints visible template-downgrade + cross-model warnings. Enforced by three h-check-sys-smoke guards (lock coverage, pre-check coverage, stale-sentinel).
web_model_switch.backup_restore: bin/h-backup-user (model marker), bin/h-restore-user (visible warnings + cross-model banner)
web_model_switch.no_symlink: new h-* commands, no v-* symlink

web_switches.description: Per-domain switches replacing selectable templates (#219): admin suspension + customer offline render from share/web/suspend/{admin,offline}/ (nginx/proxy/apache2 tpl+stpl, all three web models share one path via WEBTPL_OVERRIDE in prepare_web_domain_values); proxy caching writes a fragment into the domain's nginx.location.d/ (read inside location / of the default proxy vhost) plus one zone file per domain under /etc/nginx/conf.d/cache-zone.<domain>.conf.
web_switches.render: include/domain.sh prepare_web_domain_values + add_web_config (WEBTPL_OVERRIDE, missing-template guard with skip tally)
web_switches.http3: #613 - a per-domain switch, not a template variant. quic listen + Alt-Svc go into nginx.ssl.conf_http3, picked up by the merged SSL block's generic nginx.ssl.conf_* glob (no template/renderer change). Gate (include/domain.sh nginx_has_http3): SSL + nginx front + nginx --with-http_v3_module (deb12/ub24 OS nginx lacks it). Plain quic, no reuseport. h-change-web-domain-ip re-emits the fragment (it carries the IP, is not a .conf); restore drops it when the target nginx cannot do http3.
web_switches.flags: web.conf OFFLINE / PROXY_CACHE / PROXY_CACHE_DURATION / HTTP3 / DOCKER / DOCKER_PORT / DOCKER_OCTET - registered in syshealth_known_keys web. Since #705 the restore keeps the archived record instead of re-emitting it from a field list, so a new flag needs no restore change; only a field that must be REWRITTEN on restore belongs in the remap table there.
web_switches.guards: h-check-sys-smoke: check_web_cache_zones (flag without zone), check_vhost_nonempty (0-byte vhost)
web_switches.panel: web/edit/web/ - offline checkbox in the main form, proxy-cache block next to the FastCGI one (PROXY_SYSTEM=nginx only), HTTP/3 checkbox in the SSL section gated on session WEB_HTTP3 (computed by h-list-sys-config from nginx -V, folded into the session by inc/main.php) + an nginx front
web_switches.legacy_mapping: include/domain.sh accept_web_template + map_legacy_template - every write (CLI, restore, package) passes through; known legacy values are mapped with their side effect (caching -> cache switch, wordpress*-http3 -> base template + http3 switch), unknown ones error on the CLI and fall back on restore. Guard: check_web_templates_resolvable.
web_switches.docker_limits: #618/#619 - DOCKER_SYSTEM (hestia.conf, written by h-add-sys-docker) gates the admin switch in edit-user; docker requires an unjailed login shell, enforced in h-add-user-docker as well as the view. Package field DOCKER_LIMIT (unlimited|low|medium|high) maps to systemd properties in include/docker.sh docker_slice_properties and lands on user-<companion_uid>.slice - where the daemon AND all containers of that customer live, verified via a container cgroup path. Applied from h-add-user-docker, h-change-user-package and h-rebuild-user. companion_stop() in include/docker.sh is shared with h-delete-user-docker and the in-place restore (#615).
web_switches.docker_publishing: #566/#592 - a per-customer loopback /24 (user.conf DOCKER_IP = its .1, allocated in h-add-user-docker, daemon.json default bind with both keys) and three domain fields DOCKER (docker template name, empty = off) / DOCKER_PORT / DOCKER_OCTET. add_web_config renders the FRONT from templates/docker/<system>/ and skips the both-model apache backend; h-add-web-domain-backend removes the pool (central like PHP_VERSION=none); %docker_ip% is read via get_user_value (rebuild-safe) with the octet applied; %front_port%/%front_ssl_port% resolve the public listener so one template serves nginx-only and both. Separation: fw_restrict_docker_nets renders one output rule per customer /24 (webserver allowlisted) from the user records. Panel: edit_web checkbox + <net>._ octet + port, selectors hidden while active, plus the docker template select from h-list-web-templates-docker (front system = PROXY_SYSTEM or WEB_SYSTEM; shown only on more than one template, and docker templates never appear in the general list). Every POST family whose control the docker branch hides gates on empty($DOCKER) - reading an absent key was a fatal for the pool template and dropped PROXY on every save. Backup skips the legacy vhost lookup for a docker domain: on the both model that config cannot exist and aborted the whole user backup. Traps: wildcard listeners block the customer bind (live ss check in the add command); apache LE needs DocumentRoot + acme ProxyPass exemption BEFORE the catch-all; websocket map is global (share/nginx/websocket-upgrade.conf), per-vhost would collide.
web_switches.ssl_switches: SSL_FORCE / SSL_HSTS render as per-domain fragments the vhost includes. The fragment carries the directive of the FRONT that reads it - apache 'Header always set', nginx 'add_header' - and the apache templates include it inside the SSL vhost (#638; before that it was nginx syntax on every front and no apache include, so the switch was a silent no-op). Guard: check_web_hsts_effective flags SSL_HSTS='yes' whose fragment is missing or written for the other server.

backup_restore.description: User backup and restore. The archive is an UNCOMPRESSED outer tar (bin/h-backup-user, include/backup.sh local_backup) with per-object gzip or zstd inside, marked by a ./.zstd member; ./vesta vs ./hestia names the container. There is no version field - a foreign archive is recognised by its features, never by a marker. --numeric-owner appears NOWHERE on purpose: the account is created before anything is unpacked (rebuild_user_conf), so tar resolves the archived owner by NAME onto a freshly allocated uid (#388). That same mechanism is what lets an archive be restored under a different customer name, rewriting FTP_USER, CUSTOM_DOCROOT and the database prefixes.
backup_restore.layout: Since #789 every customer's archives sit in /backup/$user/ (0750, hestia:$user; /backup itself is 0711), the run log beside them; a hand-placed migration archive may stay flat in /backup, and backup_archive_path in include/backup.sh is the ONLY resolver of those two places - symlinks refused, messages name the spot.
backup_restore.adoption: Recording a hand-placed archive is h-add-user-backup: it probes the file and derives every record field from the CONTENT, and since #820 h-restore-user calls it at the end of a restore whenever no record names the archive - an unrecorded file inside /backup/$user/ counts as its own set in backup_set_removals and BACKUPS='1' rotates it away on the next run, while a flat one is structurally safe because the rotation only enumerates $BACKUP/$user/. ADOPTED='yes' is what protects a record's file: the rotation subtracts adopted names and h-delete-user-backup forgets the record without deleting the file. LOCAL is not a protection but a per-row display field the listers derive through the resolver (#790).
backup_restore.retention: Remote targets may retain more sets than the package (BACKUPS_KEEP per target conf, #790); the record outlives the local file - record retention follows the longest keep anywhere, file rotation per place follows its own number - so the #791 ownership bind still covers archives only a remote holds.
backup_restore.server_backup: A SERVER backup is a separate object (bin/h-backup-server): the state that belongs to the box - the shared webmail databases and /etc/roundcube, hestia.conf, the packages, the firewall sources - which no per-customer archive can carry without carrying other customers' rows. Its components are derived from what the host has, and it is restored only per named component; there is deliberately no whole-archive verb (#710).
backup_restore.content_map: Content map (#712): every archive carries hestia/backup.map, five NUL-terminated fields per entry (path, hash, mode, owner, symlink target), paths and metadata from the finished member's listing, content hashes from the live tree taken BEFORE the member is tarred (batched - per-file hashing through --to-command was 99.8% of the runtime) and joined by path, so the map is never newer than the archive and every race lands on re-ship, not on silent omission - h-list-user-backup-map reads it back.
backup_restore.differential: Differential archives (#712): BACKUPS_MODE in the package (full|diff|restic, default full) decides per customer; 'diff' rebuilds the web and mail members against the newest full archive's local map ($USER_DATA/backup-maps/), everything else stays whole, retention keeps a base as long as any kept archive names it; the base archive itself only has to be REACHABLE (local or on a configured remote's fresh listing), and the restore fetches it over the same transport chain as the archive - remote-only boxes diff too (#790 stage 3).
backup_restore.restic: h-backup-users dispatches per mode, so restic is an alternative to the archive path, not a parallel run. restic is an ADDON since #217 (h-add-sys-restic / h-delete-sys-restic, COMPONENT_ADDON_RESTIC): BACKUPS_MODE is the single truth about a customer's mode - BACKUPS_INCREMENTAL is gone, BACKUP_INCREMENTAL stays as the server switch meaning 'restic installed and a repository configured'. is_restic_repo_configured is the one gate that resolves the repository (and the separator in the composed repo path); without it an unset REPO made restic create a relative repo wherever the run started.
backup_restore.restic_lifecycle: Deleting a customer keeps their backups in every mode, so h-delete-user-backups-restic is the explicit way out (names repository, snapshot and package count first, and only acts on the consent word) and h-list-sys-backup-orphans-restic reports what is left - it walks the repository DIRECTORIES under the base, not the customer list, because a deleted customer is exactly the case it exists for, and it separates an unreadable repository from an empty one. A manual full export is not a fourth mode but one ordinary archive run (h-export-user-backup): the record carries MODE='export' plus ADOPTED='yes', which takes it out of the rotation through the mechanism operator-placed files already use, and BACKUP_EXPORT_LIMIT (default 2) REFUSES with the existing exports named instead of clearing the oldest away. Marker and limit both sit in h-backup-user and are reached by an ARGUMENT (h-backup-user USER NOTIFY yes), never an environment prefix - the consent word was made an argument for the same reason (GHSA-2xw3), and a limit in the wrapper misses every direct caller. Neither the delete command nor the orphan report accepts a REMOTE repository base: sftp: and rclone: targets are not paths, so rm -rf hits nothing while rm -f takes the packages that carry the only spare key, and a glob over such a base stays literal so the report would sweep nothing and say so only in its reach counters. restic_repo_is_local (include/main.sh) is the one predicate - only an absolute path counts as local, anything else is treated as remote because that is the safe way for a destructive command to be wrong.
backup_restore.restic_panel: In the panel the Backups tab branches on BACKUPS_MODE (web/list/backup/index.php) instead of a second button, ?archives=1 is the escape back to the archives and exports, and the mode is read there via h-list-user - $panel is built inside render_page and does not exist at that point, which is why the branch silently never fired at first. /list/backup/incremental/index.php had to join the CSRF entry-route list in web/inc/prevent_csrf.php the moment it became the tab's landing page: a request without a Referer (bookmark, outside link, return after a timeout) answers 400 otherwise, and a click inside the panel never shows it.
backup_restore.record_handling: #705: the restore takes the archived record line and edits it AS TEXT (record_set_field / record_del_field in include/backup.sh), it does not parse and re-emit it. Two reasons, both load-bearing: a re-emit from a list of known keys silently dropped every field the list did not know - AUTH_USER/AUTH_HASH, WP, DIR_LIST, CROWDSEC, BOTLIMIT - and the FIELD ORDER matters, because include/botpolicy.sh reads DOMAIN first and BOTLIMIT behind it with sed. Only the fields in the remap table are rewritten; everything else survives untouched, including fields added later. It fires only when the domain is NEW on the target, which is why it never showed in testing and always shows in migration and disaster recovery.
backup_restore.trust_boundary: record_line_valid (include/backup.sh) gates every verbatim append - web, db and mail. The line must be exactly KEY='VALUE' separated by single spaces; ' " \ ` and newline are refused, $ is allowed because MD5/AUTH_HASH/STATS_CRYPT are crypt hashes. It is needed because the consumers downstream do not all go through the PHP tokenizer: botpolicy and crowdsec read with sed on quote boundaries, get_object_value with grep/cut, and the h-list-* emitters splice into JSON. It also lets record_set_field find a field with a plain " KEY='" search, which is only unambiguous while ' is banned from values.
backup_restore.dkim: Archive mail/<domain>/hestia/<domain>.pem -> $USER_DATA/mail/<domain>.pem -> conf/mail/<domain>/dkim.pem -> /etc/exim4/domains/<domain>/dkim.pem (symlink) -> exim DKIM_FILE dsearch, selector fixed to 'mail'. No regeneration branch is reachable from a restore, and that is deliberate: the published TXT record lives on a nameserver we do not run, so a new key would not match it. A record saying DKIM='yes' with no .pem is a NAMED failure in rebuild_mail_domain_conf (#705) - it used to be a cp error on stderr while the panel kept showing DKIM on and every message failed DKIM instead of merely being unsigned.
not_written: dns/ - never produced; a foreign archive's dns/ member is ignored on restore
template/ per web domain - removed, nothing ever read it back
htpasswd - not archived at all; the AUTH_USER/AUTH_HASH record fields are the only source
backup_restore.plan: backup-restore-plan.md on the docs branch; umbrella issue #240, stages #703-#713 + #342
backup_restore.probe: #707: the archive is read ONCE before anything is written. backup_probe (include/backup.sh) describes what is IN the file - container, codec, object names per subsystem, dns zones, packages - and extracts the record members so nothing has to unpack it a second time; backup_report compares that against THIS host and says what will be lost or rewritten. Two functions because the first is about the file alone and the second only means anything against a particular box. Everything is derived, including the set of record keys this host itself can write, which is the registry plus the live records plus what any add_object_key call in bin/ could add - each of those three alone shrinks in a way that would make the report lie. An empty report is PRINTED, never left as silence.
backup_restore.probe_consumers: bin/h-list-backup-contents (reads the FILE, so an archive with no backup.conf record - a HestiaCP one placed by hand - is inspectable at all), and the preflight in h-restore-user. The panel dialog is the third, still to come. One wording, one function, so the three cannot drift.

notification_mta.description: The MTA that carries panel and CLI notification mail (#872, #192). Everything goes through web/inc/mail-wrapper.php - that is $SENDMAIL in include/main.sh - which calls send_email() and, unless USE_SERVER_SMTP points at a relay, PHPMailer's mail(), i.e. PHP's sendmail_path. So a box without /usr/sbin/sendmail loses every notification while the wrapper still exits 0. With a mail block the MTA comes from install_mail (exim4-daemon-heavy plus the HestiaRE exim template); without one, install_exim_sendonly installs exim4-daemon-light and configure_exim_sendonly puts Debian's own update-exim4.conf machinery into send-only shape (dc_eximconfig_configtype=internet, dc_local_interfaces loopback) - the HestiaRE template is deliberately NOT used there. light rather than heavy because send-only needs no lookups or authenticators; a box that later gains a mail block gets heavy, which replaces light. Gated by COMPONENT_PANEL_EXIM, which until #872 was written by the wizard and read by nobody; when it is off the installer LOOKS at USE_SERVER_SMTP/SERVER_SMTP_HOST rather than claiming a relay, and warns when there is none: the send-only branch only configured and presumed the package, so a nomail box had an MTA solely when the base image happened to ship one - Debian does, Ubuntu does not. h-check-sys-smoke check_notification_mta asserts the binary PHP will actually call, and check_exim_sendonly now says out loud when it cannot verify the routing instead of returning silently.

panel_port.description: Panel port (#730). The port lives in the Panel-Caddy site (/etc/caddy/hestia.conf `https://:PORT` plus the listener-wrapper block in /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, scoped to the panel port so it does not wrap the loopback webmail listeners); BACKEND_PORT in hestia.conf is what everything else follows - the firewall HESTIA rule and chain, the Roundcube/Tachyon password plugins, and the phpMyAdmin proxy include on every customer domain (%panel_port% in share/{nginx/apps/phpmyadmin.inc,apache2/apps/phpmyadmin.conf}, rendered by h-change-sys-db-alias). h-change-sys-port moves all of them and reads the CURRENT port from the caddy site, not from BACKEND_PORT: it used to rewrite $HESTIA/nginx/conf/nginx.conf, a file that has not existed since the Caddy switch, so any port but 8083 wrote the config and the firewall while Caddy kept listening on the old one. The reserved set in include/ports.sh is DERIVED from the shipped listener declarations under share/ and include/, minus the port the panel's own site template declares - so a listener added later cannot fall out of the set. It is NOT a numeric band: it measures out at about a dozen individual ports, the 80xx of panel and web stack but also 3306 from share/mysql/my-*.cnf, 5432 from include/db.sh and 4190 from our managesieve config. A digit class limited to 8xxx let 3306 through as a panel port and MariaDB then could not bind an hour later. The scan is anchored on declaration forms (listen, a loopback target, a site address, port=/*_PORT=) and drops three measured classes of noise: comment lines (dovecot and rspamd ship 11333/9900/2000 commented out), application code (*.php), where a listener is not declared and vendored code carries other people's ports - adminer connects to localhost:1433; VENDORED.json cannot do that job because it is export-ignore and never reaches a box, and IP octets. An empty scan refuses instead of accepting everything. The move proves itself: the listener is written and restarted FIRST, and only when the new port actually answers do BACKEND_PORT, the firewall and the proxies follow - if it does not, the caddy files are rolled back and nothing else was touched. The wizard validates before the first write (range 1024-65535, reserved set, live holder named); the installer no longer swallows a failed apply; h-check-sys-smoke check_panel_port compares the caddy site against BACKEND_PORT.
